key_idea: Build a graph from a triangle-free 'hole' relation realized through random tensors and bilinear forms over F_2, and show via entropy minimization, containers, and Fourier/Walsh estimates that any dense unit law produces many pairs with all four cross holes; this supersaturation forces small clique minors.
reason: The high-level reduction (supersaturation plus containers, giving alpha ≤ 2 and a small clique minor) is sensible, but it sits under a huge stack of peeling, pinning, phase alternatives, compactness limits and parameter ledgers, so the reason the result holds is hard to see. The proof is intricate, with many cases (three prepared alternatives, a phase dichotomy, inverse-polynomial options) and a lot of bookkeeping, far beyond what any reader could hold in their head.
